prompt: What does the lesson say the OWASP LLM Top 10 is good for?
hint: Think of a reviewer's comment on a pull request.

choices.text: A checklist that marks an application as covered
choices.why: Each entry is a family of failures; ticking names says nothing about a feature.

choices.text: A shared vocabulary for naming the ways software fails
choices.why: Right: one name, the same failure in everyone's head.

choices.text: A ranking to memorise for interviews
choices.why: The numbers change between editions.

choices.text: A legal standard the ANPD enforces
choices.why: It is a community document, not a law.

prompt: An assistant with no tools is being reviewed. Why is ticking all ten entries the wrong exercise?
hint: Exposure depends on what the application does.

choices.text: Each entry weighs differently for this assistant
choices.why: Right: each entry is a question for this application.

choices.text: Assistants without tools are outside the OWASP list
choices.why: They are inside it; some entries simply weigh less.

choices.text: Only the first five entries apply to assistants
choices.why: Nothing in the list divides it that way.

choices.text: Ticking is right, but it must be done every month
choices.why: Frequency does not fix a checklist that asks nothing.

prompt: The edition of the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications that this lesson uses is from ___.
Match each OWASP category to the lesson whose control covers it in this course.
hint: One lesson on the right covers none of these.

prompt: Why does the Prompt Injection row name three controls rather than one?

choices.text: Three is the number OWASP requires for every category
choices.why: No such rule.

choices.text: No single control removes the root
choices.why: Right: narrow the input, filter the output, gate the tools.

choices.text: Each control covers one language
choices.why: Language has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: The lab could not decide which one works
choices.why: Each does a different job; none is enough alone.

prompt: Which category does the lab cover only with a canary, and what does that miss?

choices.text: System Prompt Leakage, because a paraphrase carries no marker
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Misinformation: a canary does not check numbers
choices.why: Misinformation is covered by guard ground, not a canary.

choices.text: Supply Chain: a canary does not see packages
choices.why: Supply chain is covered by guard deps.

choices.text: Unbounded Consumption: a canary does not count calls
choices.why: That row has three limits, none of them a canary.

prompt: Which controls from this course appear in the Unbounded Consumption row? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: per-user rate limits, lesson 17
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: the retry cap, lesson 19
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: the call budget of the tool gate, lesson 20
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: the retention sweep, lesson 21
choices.why: That bounds how long data is kept, not what is spent.

prompt: How many of the ten categories have at least one control in the lab?
A row of the map names a command. What does that establish, according to the lesson?

choices.text: That the category cannot happen in the application
choices.why: A control reduces a risk; it does not remove the category.

choices.text: That OWASP has certified the command
choices.why: OWASP certifies nothing here.

choices.text: A control exists; enough is another matter
choices.why: Right: a row is a pointer, not a proof.

choices.text: That the category can be dropped from future reviews
choices.why: It is asked again for every feature.

prompt: Which two categories have no control in this lab? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Data and Model Poisoning
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Excessive Agency
choices.why: Covered by the tool gate.

choices.text: Misinformation
choices.why: Covered by guard ground.

prompt: Tarefa's assistant retrieves only three help centre pages written by Tarefa. What should the review write for Vector and Embedding Weaknesses?
hint: A small exposure is still a row.

choices.text: Nothing, since the exposure is small
choices.why: A row left empty is the gap the lesson warns about.

choices.text: A tick, since Tarefa wrote the pages
choices.why: Writing the pages is not a control on the store.

choices.text: A control from lesson 19, since it checks outputs
choices.why: The schema checks replies, not the store they draw on.

choices.text: N/A or accepted, with reason and date
choices.why: Right: so the row is looked at again when retrieval grows.

prompt: Put a review of a new feature against the list in order.
hint: Rows first, answers next, then the record.
items: Take the ten categories as rows
For each, name a control, mark not applicable with a reason, or accept the risk
Write who accepted each risk and until when
Keep the review beside the code and revisit it when the feature or the list changes

prompt: What changed in the 2025 edition compared with 2023, according to the lesson?
hint: Two entries were added and one was renamed.

choices.text: The list was cut from ten entries to five
choices.why: It still has ten.

choices.text: Two entries were added, and one was renamed
choices.why: Right: system prompt leakage and vector weaknesses came in, and misinformation replaced overreliance.

choices.text: Prompt injection was removed as solved
choices.why: It is LLM01 in 2025.

choices.text: The numbers were frozen so that they stay put
choices.why: The lesson expects them to change again.

prompt: Match each one-line meaning to its OWASP category.
hint: One name on the right is not one of the ten.

pairs.left: an agent can do more than its task needs
one user or one loop spends without limit
a reply is used by other code without being checked

prompt: A reviewer marks Excessive Agency as not applicable for a feature that summarises tickets, and writes no reason. What is missing?
hint: When should the row be looked at again?

choices.text: Nothing, since summaries need no tools
choices.why: The reason is what makes the answer revisitable.

choices.text: A control from lesson 20, which has to be named
choices.why: Not applicable is a valid answer when the reason is written.

choices.text: Why it does not apply, to revisit later
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A canary, since summaries can leak
choices.why: Leakage is another row.
